title: Native Shell — Build once, native everywhere | Rust UI framework
description: Native Shell is a Rust-first native UI framework: build one app for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux and the web, with each platform’s own UI and interaction.
lead: Write only TSX and ship native clients that keep pace with Rust. One codebase runs on 8 platforms, each with the system’s own UI and interaction.
idle: Your app sits in the middle. Each arch around it is a platform.
numbersTitle: A client written in TSX, right beside Rust
numbersLead: In NSH only your app’s code is JS. The reactive graph, the renderer, layout and every module are Rust. TSX and Rust apps share the same native execution pipeline.

numbersNote: Release builds. Memory at rest: macOS footprint on an Apple M3 (the counter app and the Rust template at 1200 × 800; the system window holds one label at 480 × 640); Linux private dirty memory on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (nsh init’s TSX and Rust templates and a GTK window with one label, all at 480 × 640); Windows private working set. Each platform’s measure, with RSS and USS, is in the report. Sizes: nsh package’s release builds, with link-time optimization and stripped; the TSX executable holds the QuickJS runtime, the app’s code is under 1 KB; the package is the zipped .app on macOS, the .tar.gz on Linux and the .zip on Windows; on the web, what the browser downloads, runtime and app.

viewsTitle: 8 platforms, each with the system’s own controls
viewsLead: NSH builds each UI from what its platform already has. Text input, selection, input methods and accessibility come from the system, and what a new OS release brings to them reaches the app with it.
embedNote: Maps, web views, video and any native view the host registers are one more subview in the same hierarchy: they lay out, clip, scroll and take touches with the rest of the app.
formTitle: One app, in each device’s own form
formLead: The same compiled code runs twice here, and only the device differs. With a pointer it is a window with its conversations at the side; on a phone the buttons and the composer float in Liquid Glass with the thread scrolling beneath; in a terminal it sits on the character grid. The app is written once.
formCaption: Desktop and phone run live in your browser on Native Shell’s web runtime. The terminal is real output of nsh run --target tui.
pending: The live preview is not built yet: run bun run dev (or cargo xtask web).
langTitle: The same engine in Rust, when you want it
langLead: Rust is a first-class language for whole apps: UI, logic and components compile to native code, ready for demanding business logic. Both use the same elements and signals, and TSX screens import your Rust components.
fastTitle: Only the views that changed are touched
fastLead: Every element is a view the platform keeps. A change runs only the expressions that read the changed signal, in one batch per frame. The main thread never waits for JS and native animations run without it, so scrolling and animation hold 120 FPS and the app sits near idle at rest.
fastLegend: The two texts that read the signals change and the history gains a row; no other view is touched.
shipTitle: After release, your app can still take new UI
shipLead: Your team can write it, or a model can generate it for each request. It reaches the device as a signed module, runs in a sandbox the host sets, and shows natively.

flow.title: Write
flow.body: Your team or a model writes a TSX module.

flow.title: Check
flow.body: Type-check it, then run its tests headless.

flow.title: Sign
flow.body: An Ed25519-signed .nshpkg, its release key certified by an offline root.

flow.title: Run
flow.body: The device verifies the signature, certificate and revocations. Each view gets a VM with memory, call-time and node limits, and only the capabilities the host grants.

waysHead: Three ways to ship, one engine
foundTitle: Behavior from NSH, the look from you
foundLead: nsh/base holds unstyled base components that own state, focus, keyboard and accessibility, and the app styles every part. One nsh command line does the rest.
kitNote: , from the same Longbridge team, is a ready-to-use UI component library for macOS, Windows and Linux. Much of NSH's design comes from GPUI Kit, and apps built with NSH embed directly in GPUI Kit apps.
closeBody: Install nsh and have your first TSX app running in a minute.

ways.label: Standalone apps
ways.body: Write it in Rust, TSX or both, and package an installable iOS, Android, macOS, Windows or Linux app, or a static website.

ways.label: Dynamic UI and plugins
ways.body: Embed a view on any screen and load signed TSX modules into it at run time, next to the host’s own native components.

ways.label: AI-generated UI
ways.body: A model writes a module per request, so the app answers with an interface. Your server checks and signs it.

found.title: Unstyled base components
found.body: Navigation, dialogs, menus, popovers, tabs, selects, data tables, a code editor and a rich text kernel. Style every part with Tailwind classes or typed styles.

found.title: One toolchain, for people and agents
found.body: One nsh executable creates, builds, type-checks, hot-reloads, tests, packages and signs. Declarations are generated from the Rust sources and the docs are served as llms.txt, so an agent runs the whole loop with the same commands.

found.title: Checked on every target
found.body: The same tests run headless, and in real windows, an iOS simulator, an Android device or a browser, with the platform’s own input.
